answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a bond in a vault, with the bond doubling for every additional identity funded from the same on-chain source, detected by clustering funding transactions. A lone operator spinning up a sable army of sockpuppets faces a bond that doubles with each one, so the tenth identity costs 512 times the first, and the cost curve keeps rising past any horizon of cheap bulk creation. Honest newcomers pay only the base bond, while the doubling rule makes mass fabrication ruinous before it starts.
